title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #1 (Term 1)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What happens to a dead plant? (1 mark)
   A. It flies away
   B. It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   C. It turns into an animal
   D. It becomes a rock

2. In which part do you find the seeds of a mango? (1 mark)
   A. Root
   B. Stem
   C. Fruit
   D. Leaf

3. A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants (1 mark)
   A. need no water
   B. respond to light
   C. walk
   D. make sound

4. A plant on a windowsill grows towards the window. What is it responding to? (1 mark)
   A. Soil colour
   B. Wind speed
   C. Light
   D. Sound

5. Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school? (1 mark)
   A. Water them when the soil is dry
   B. Throw litter on them
   C. Trample on flower beds
   D. Pick all the flowers

6. Which of these shows a plant reproducing? (1 mark)
   A. A stem getting taller
   B. A leaf turning green
   C. A root drinking water
   D. A bean plant making pods with seeds

7. Why do animals need to feed? (1 mark)
   A. To grow feathers only
   B. To make noise
   C. To get energy and to grow
   D. To make their skin colourful

8. Which of these animals gives birth to live young? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Hen
   C. Housefly
   D. Frog

9. Which of these statements is true? (1 mark)
   A. All animals have six legs
   B. All animals can fly
   C. All small animals are insects
   D. All fish have a backbone

10. How do young mammals get their first food? (1 mark)
   A. By hunting
   B. By eating stones
   C. By drinking their mother's milk
   D. By eating grass

11. Which of these can you use to find out the differences between vertebrates and invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Only guesses
   B. Noise
   C. Books and digital sources
   D. Weather

12. Which group of vertebrates has feathers? (1 mark)
   A. Birds
   B. Reptiles
   C. Amphibians
   D. Fish

13. Which group of animals has dry, scaly skin and includes snakes and crocodiles? (1 mark)
   A. Amphibians
   B. Mammals
   C. Reptiles
   D. Birds

14. Which food group helps to prevent constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   B. Sweets
   C. Fizzy drinks
   D. Sugary biscuits

15. Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks? (1 mark)
   A. They make teeth stronger
   B. They make you taller
   C. They cause tooth decay
   D. They help digestion

16. What do teeth do in digestion? (1 mark)
   A. Digest food into the blood
   B. Cut and grind food into small pieces
   C. Take back water
   D. Store waste

17. Which of these is a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Only sweets
   B. Only soda
   C. Only tea
   D. Ugali, vegetables and beans

18. Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. A headache only
   B. Sunburn
   C. Sneezing
   D. Stomach ache

19. Which of these is a good use of a school deworming day? (1 mark)
   A. Give them to animals
   B. Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   C. Throw them away
   D. Refuse to take them

20. What is absorption? (1 mark)
   A. Chewing food
   B. Digested food passing into the blood
   C. Swallowing food
   D. Passing faeces

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe what happens to food in the stomach. (3 marks)

22. Describe what happens in the small intestine and why it is important. (4 marks)

23. Explain how a frog is similar to and different from a fish. (4 marks)

24. Write the function of the rectum and anus. (3 marks)

25. Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower. (4 marks)

26. Explain why plants are called living things. (3 marks)

27. Draw a table with two columns headed vertebrates and invertebrates. Place these animals correctly: goat, butterfly, snake, snail, hen, spider. (5 marks)

28. Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — It rots and returns nutrients to the soil
   Dead plants decay and give nutrients back to the soil.

2. C — Fruit
   Seeds are found inside fruits.

3. B — respond to light
   The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

4. C — Light
   Plants bend and grow towards light coming from one side.

5. A — Water them when the soil is dry
   Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

6. D — A bean plant making pods with seeds
   Making seeds is reproduction. Growing taller is growth.

7. C — To get energy and to grow
   Food gives animals energy and materials for growth.

8. A — Goat
   Goats are mammals and give birth to live young. Hens, frogs and flies lay eggs.

9. D — All fish have a backbone
   Fish are vertebrates. Small animals may be spiders, worms or others.

10. C — By drinking their mother's milk
   Mammals feed their babies with milk.

11. C — Books and digital sources
   We can search print and digital media for information.

12. A — Birds
   Only birds have feathers.

13. C — Reptiles
   Reptiles have dry, scaly skin.

14. A — Fibre in fruits and vegetables
   Fibre helps food move through the intestines.

15. C — They cause tooth decay
   Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

16. B — Cut and grind food into small pieces
   Chewing makes food smaller.

17. D — Ugali, vegetables and beans
   A balanced meal has energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.

18. D — Stomach ache
   Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

19. B — Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   Follow the health worker's advice.

20. B — Digested food passing into the blood
   Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: The stomach churns the food and mixes it with strong juices. The juices kill many germs and break down the food into a thick soup.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for churns, 1 mark for juices and 1 mark for germs or thick soup.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Digestion is finished there. Digested food passes through the wall into the blood. The blood carries it to all parts of the body for energy, growth and repair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Both are vertebrates and have a backbone. A frog has moist skin and lives on land and in water, and a fish lives in water and has gills and fins.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for similarity and 2 marks for differences.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: They show signs of life. They grow, reproduce, remove waste, respond to changes and die.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying they show signs of life and 2 marks for correct signs given.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat, snake, hen. Invertebrates: butterfly, snail, spider.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the table and 4 marks for placing the six animals (award 1 mark for two correct).

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four items.
